name: libmikmod
why: A tracker-module playback library for old MOD files, a door into the 90s demoscene sound world.

brief.what_it_is: libmikmod is a portable sound library for playing tracker music modules. It reads module files in many formats, including MOD, S3M, IT and XM, and renders them to audio through one of several output drivers. The homepage also describes the MikMod module player, which is a separate program built on the library. The page says the player began on MS-DOS and was later ported to Unix, Macintosh, BeOS and Java. The scout note frames it as MOD-only, but the homepage says the format list is much wider.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit motivation. It describes MikMod as a module player and library that supports many formats, and it credits a long list of authors and maintainers, which suggests a long-running preservation and maintenance effort.
brief.how_it_works: The changelogs describe per-format loaders (for example IT, XM, S3M, STM, AMF, MED and UMX), decompressors for packed modules, and a pluggable output layer. The output layer includes drivers for ALSA, OSS, PulseAudio, SDL, OpenAL, WASAPI, WebAudio and Android, plus file writers for WAV, AIFF and raw PCM. The homepage itself does not describe the internal design.
brief.install_notes: The homepage shows no installation steps. It links to release tarballs on SourceForge under libmikmod/<version>/. The changelogs mention autotools, CMake, standalone makefiles (MinGW, Open Watcom, djgpp, OS/2) and a configure option --disable-alldrv that turns off all audio output drivers. I did not see the libmikmod-config executable described on the pages I read.
brief.standout: It is a tracker-format library still getting releases decades after the formats were current, and its changelogs show a steady stream of fixes for malformed or crafted module files, some with CVE numbers. It also ships output drivers for unusual targets such as Dreamcast, Nintendo 64, PlayStation Vita and AmigaOS.
brief.status: maintained. The homepage lists libmikmod 3.3.15 and 3.1.25 dated October 10 2026, and 3.3.14 and the player 3.2.10 dated September 11 2026, all described as bug-fix releases with upgrades recommended. The page says the maintainer role passed to Ozkan in September 2013.
brief.caveats: I read only the homepage, and the fetch was cut at 40000 characters, so the rest of the changelog and any documentation were not seen. No install or build commands appeared. The brew caveats field is empty. The page mentions older libmikmod2 (3.1.x) releases that still get fixes, so version choice matters. Some listed platform support (for example BeOS and OS/2) is historical and may not be current.
quotes: Mikmod is a module player and library supporting many formats, including mod, s3m, it, and xm.
Originally a player for MS-DOS, MikMod has been ported to other platforms, such as Unix, Macintosh, BeOS, and Java(!!)
This is a bug fix/maintenance release for the current libmikmod3 series.  Upgrading is highly recommended.
